source_text: Quod cum Deus parvulis nihil de proprio tam boni quam mali merentibus gloriam regenerationis attribuit, hoc ipso eos ad suam curam, ad suum ius, ad suum dominium pertinere docet, quod eorum voluntatem ineffabilis praevenit beneficii largitate
pass_a_gloss: That/which when/with God little-ones nothing about/from proprio so of-good than/which of-evil merentibus gloriam of-regeneration attribuit, this ipso them to his-own why, to his-own ius, to his-own of-the-Lord pertinere docet, that/which their will ineffabilis praevenit beneficii by-bounty.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: When God grants the glory of regeneration to infants who have deserved neither good nor evil by anything of their own, he teaches by that very act that they belong to his care, his right, and his dominion: he anticipates their will with the lavish gift of an inexpressible benefit.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
